high.title: HOSE Announces 67 Stock Codes Cut from Margin Trading in May
high.summary: HoSE has announced an additional list of securities not eligible for margin trading. AAN (A An Food Corporation) was removed from margin eligibility due to being listed for less than 6 months. The stock debuted on May 22 at 15,000 VND and closed at 19,250 VND on May 25, up 6.9%. VAF was removed from the margin cut list as it was delisted. As of May 22, 2026, HOSE has cut margin trading for 67 stock codes. This margin reduction affects market liquidity and trader sentiment, as it limits leverage opportunities for institutional and retail investors, potentially reducing trading volumes in affected stocks.

high.title: Money Flowing into Securities Hits 2-Month Low, What's Happening?
high.summary: Despite VN-Index gaining 9 points to 1,886 on May 25, the broader market showed weakness with 174 declining stocks vs 129 advancing on HoSE. Most critically, trading liquidity plummeted to under 13,900 billion VND, the lowest in nearly 2 months since April 7. This divergence between index performance and market breadth indicates selective buying in large-cap stocks while general investor sentiment remains cautious. The weak liquidity suggests money is concentrating in few blue-chip stocks rather than broad market participation, creating challenges for short-term profit opportunities and signaling underlying market uncertainty that could pressure the VND and affect foreign investment flows.

high.title: What to See from SBV's Move to Strengthen Inspection of Interest Rate Reductions by Commercial Banks?
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) is strengthening inspections of commercial banks' interest rate reduction compliance, demonstrating determination to combat the "silent" rate increases at some banks recently. This move aims to stabilize market interest rate levels to support businesses and citizens. However, SBV faces challenging monetary policy management amid complex global economic and geopolitical developments. With major central banks (Fed, ECB, BOE) maintaining rates and some (Australia, Ireland, Philippines) raising rates in early 2026, SBV must balance domestic growth support with external pressures. This inspection intensification signals SBV's commitment to keeping rates accommodative despite global tightening trends, which should support VND stability and domestic credit growth while potentially pressuring the exchange rate if global rate differentials widen.

high.title: Unprecedented Event in Vietnam Banking History: What's Happening?
high.summary: By end-January 2026, individual deposits in the banking system reached a historic high of over 10.3 trillion VND, up 0.45% from end-2025 and representing an increase of nearly 3.2 trillion VND year-over-year. Meanwhile, corporate and institutional deposits fell 1.62% to just over 6 trillion VND. Credit outstanding reached approximately 19.4 trillion VND by mid-May 2026, up 18.3% year-over-year, while deposit mobilization reached about 18 trillion VND, up 14.9%. This unprecedented shift shows individuals are increasingly saving while businesses are borrowing, indicating strong domestic liquidity but potential corporate financial stress. The deposit surge supports VND stability and gives banks ample funding for credit growth, but the corporate deposit decline may signal business confidence issues that could affect economic growth and currency stability.

medium.title: Thai Investors Withdraw Capital from 2 Leading ETFs in Vietnam
medium.summary: Foreign selling continues as a persistent trend on Vietnam's stock market, with over 62,000 billion VND net sold on HoSE since early 2026. Thai investors have significantly reduced holdings in DCVFM VN30 ETF and DCVFM VNDiamond ETF through depository receipts, with E1VFVN30 units falling to 90.4 million (lowest in years) and FUEVFVND declining by 10.9 million units. This withdrawal adds pressure to Vietnam's equity market and could affect VND demand.

medium.title: Banks Issue Warnings About Increasingly Sophisticated Online Fraud
medium.summary: LPBank warned about sophisticated fraud schemes involving fake labor export services targeting overseas job seekers. Fraudsters impersonate recruitment companies offering jobs in Germany, Japan, Korea, and Taiwan, requesting personal information and fees while installing malicious apps to steal banking credentials. This trend threatens digital banking security and could impact consumer confidence in electronic payment systems.

medium.title: SJC Gold, Plain Gold Ring Prices Evening of May 26
medium.summary: Gold prices dropped 500,000 VND/tael across the board. SJC gold bars now trade at 158.5-161.5 million VND/tael, with gold rings at 158.0-161.0 million VND/tael. International gold fell $32/oz to $4,537. The domestic-international price gap remains over 16 million VND/tael, continuing to reflect supply constraints and affecting capital allocation between gold and other assets including foreign currency.

medium.title: VietABank Prepares to Increase Capital
medium.summary: VietABank's board approved a capital increase plan for the first phase of 2026, issuing over 122.45 million shares to existing shareholders at a 15% ratio from retained earnings and capital reserves. The move would increase charter capital from 8,164 billion VND to approximately 9,388 billion VND, strengthening the bank's capital adequacy ratio and lending capacity.

medium.title: Savings Interest Rates Reach High Levels
medium.summary: Multiple banks launched high-interest savings programs with VIB offering up to 8.35%/year for 6-11 month terms, Sacombank over 8%/year for 6-12 months, and VPBank, SeABank maintaining 8.5-8.9%/year for medium-long terms. This aggressive rate competition indicates banks' urgent need to attract deposits amid liquidity pressures, potentially supporting VND stability but pressuring bank margins.
